headline: Messi delivers master class in final Argentina match, scores goal, assists two in 3-0 win
summary: The 39-year-old captain ended his 21-year international career in a national celebration, leaving as Argentina's most-capped player and record scorer with 126 goals.
details: Lionel Messi delivered one last master class in blue and white on Tuesday, bringing the curtain down on his extraordinary 21-year international career. He scored one goal and set up two others in a 3-0 friendly win over Benin.
The 39-year-old's final bow in front of more than 85,000 fans at a packed Monumental stadium was less about football and more a national celebration of Messi's immense service to the national team.

Landmarks across the capital glowed with Argentina's iconic sky blue and white colours. Fireworks lit up the skies above the heaving stadium as fans poured their hearts into a rendition of the national anthem.

Messi's family watched proudly from the stands alongside some of Argentina's World Cup winners from 1978, 1986, and 2022. Hours earlier, a massive No. 10 shirt emblazoned with "Gracias" was unfurled in his hometown of Rosario.

As the team bus travelled from the training centre bearing his name, Messi wiped away tears as thousands lined the route. Benin's captain looked lost for words as he handed Messi a gift and letter during the pre-match handshake.

After a goalless first half, Messi supplied the assist for Nicolas Otamendi to tap home Argentina's opener. Otamendi, who shared 17 years with Messi in the national team, was also ending his international career.

Messi then set up Nico Paz, one of the players seen as a potential successor for Argentina's No. 10 shirt, to score the second goal. In a fairytale ending, Messi converted a penalty for 3-0, his 126th international goal, prompting another round of "Messi, Messi" chants.

At the final whistle, teammates, opponents, and the referee gathered around Messi for embraces before a drone show lit up the sky. Messi leaves as the country's most-capped player (208) and record scorer.

He transformed years of frustration on the international stage into a story of World Cup and Copa America triumphs. For years, Argentina asked Messi to deliver; on Tuesday, it simply came to say "Thank You".

headline_marked: [[Shoe garland hung on Bir Shrestha Hamidur Rahman sculpture]] in Jhenaidah, sparking anger
headline: Shoe garland hung on Bir Shrestha Hamidur Rahman sculpture in Jhenaidah, sparking anger
summary: Unknown individuals desecrated the under-construction sculpture of the Liberation War hero, prompting widespread public outrage and a police investigation. The incident has drawn strong condemnation across the district.
details: Unknown individuals have hung a garland of shoes on the under-construction sculpture of Bir Shrestha Hamidur Rahman in Jhenaidah. This act of desecration has sparked widespread anger among locals and led to a police investigation.

Photos of the shoes draped over the sculpture at the central bus terminal area quickly spread on social media on Tuesday morning. The shoes were removed by midday, according to freedom fighter Kamaluzzaman, a leader of the district's Muktijoddha Sangsad.

Jhenaidah Sadar Police chief Md Asaduzzaman confirmed that police initiated an investigation after learning of the incident through Facebook. A meeting was held at the District Commissioner's office, where police were instructed to take legal action.

Bir Shrestha Hamidur Rahman, a native of Jhenaidah, was posthumously awarded Bangladesh's highest military honour for his supreme sacrifice. He was killed on October 28, 1971, during combat against Pakistani forces in Kamalganj, Moulvibazar, during the 1971 Liberation War.
